executor_description:
The FHIR List resource defines a collection of records that can be used within many places. Epic supports direct reading of the List resource to give access to Patient Lists, which includes My Lists and System Lists. To pull a My List, it must be the My List of the user whom the API call is made on behalf of or shared with that user.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed.

FHIR Errors come in two flavors:

  • Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system.
  • Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.
Error CodeSeverityDescriptionExample

4101WarningResource request returns no resultsA request for data that was otherwise valid but no information was documented or found (i.e. a patient with no pertinent implanted devices, or a demographic search where no patients met the search criteria).

The List (Problem List) API is used to represent a list of the patient’s current problems and conditions. For more details about a specific problem or condition, you can use the Condition.Read (Problems) (R4) web service.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. The medications in the list are categorized based on when the patient was supposed to be taking them relative to that encounter. The status for medication orders. By default, active is assumed. Active must be present in all searches (you cannot search for just completed meds). In the Netherlands, all statuses are returned by default and active does not have to be present in all searches. Supported statuses:  on-hold completed stopped active
The FHIR patient ID. Either this element or Patient is required.

The read interaction enables the look up of a MedicationRequest resource by a constant server ID. The read interaction is typically used to: Retrieve specific MedicationRequest data that was referenced in another resource. Initiate a contextual launch where the runtime context is a specific MedicationRequest. This resource can return various types of medications, including inpatient-ordered medications, clinic-administered medications (CAMS), patient-reported medications, and reconciled medications from Care Everywhere and other external sources. The R4 version of this resource also returns patient-reported medications. Previously, patient-reported medications were not returned by the STU3 version of MedicationRequest and needed to be queried using the STU3 MedicationStatement resource. This is no longer the case. The R4 version of this resource returns patient-reported medications with the reportedBoolean element set to True. If the informant is known, it is also specified in the reportedReference element. A user or staff member accessing this FHIR resource must have security to view medications. A MyChart user accessing this FHIR resource must be authorized to view medications in MyChart.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. executor_description:
The Observation (Activities of Daily Living) resource returns information about a patient’s last known physical and mental capabilities such as walking, bathing, and eating. Data represents the last known functional and mental statuses documented in flowsheets or inpatient goals per encounter. Information returned is further restricted to records specified by the Epic organization in profile variables. The $lastn interaction shares much with the standard Search interaction, but serves a more specific function by returning the most recent results of a particular category for a patient. If multiple instances of the same assessment or goal have been recorded for the patient, only the most recent is returned by $lastn. The following SNOMED categories are supported; both codes are currently always returned for activies of daily living observations: 118228005-Functional finding 384821006-Mental state, behavior and/or psychosocial function finding For example, if the category is 384821006, the $lastn operation will return each of the most recent mental state, behavior and/or psychosocial functional findings documented in flowsheets or inpatient goals for the patient, such as a neurological assessment or a goal to alleviate depressive symptoms. If multiple assessments or goals have the same effective datetime, and are also the most recent, $lastn returns all instances that have that datetime.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. The FHIR Observation.Create (Vitals) resource can file to all flowsheet rows, including vital signs. This resource can file vital signs for all flowsheets. When a patient-facing app uses this API, it writes to patient-entered flowsheets. If an ID is included in the request, an error is returned. The server assigns an ID to the newly created resource. executor_description:
The Observation (Vitals) resource represents component-level data for vital signs. The $lastn operation is much like the search interaction, but serves a more specific function by returning the most recent vitals readings of each type of reading for a patient. For example, if the query is for the last 3 readings (via max=3 parameter) of height, weight, and blood pressure (via the code parameter), This is different from other FHIR requests (like using the _count parameter or searching on category) because this operation is guaranteed to return results from each code. While simply getting the 5 most recent vitals readings might return only temperature readings, for example, use of the $lastn operation ensures that the most recent vitals readings for each code are returned (height, weight, blood pressure). This is useful to obtain summary data pertaining to a category. LOINC code, CADSR code, flowsheet ID, or encoded flowsheet ID. Either this element or category must be provided, but not both.  The code element value varies depending upon what is passed (for example, a flowsheet ID vs. a LOINC code). If using a flowsheet ID, the system value is different between Epic organizations, and it is also different between production and non-production environments for the same organization.
The date range for when the observation was taken.  For growth chart data (Epic version August 2021 and later), only the most recent observation within the timeframe is returned.
Reference to a patient resource the observation is about. Either this element or subject must be provided. If both are provided, they must match.

This includes any data found in the patient's flowsheets across all encounters. This resource can be queried by a combination of patient ID and vital sign LOINC code(s). The Observation resource corresponds to the following Common Clinical Data Set (CCDS) Elements: Vital Signs. The Read interaction enables the look up of an Observation resource by a constant server ID. The Observation (Labs) resource returns component level data for lab results. Observation is not normally used on its own to access lab results, because it is limited to reading microbiology sensitivities (method level, isolate level, and sensitivity level) and textual (narrative and impression) Observations. Instead, a system queries the DiagnosticReport resource to identify all lab procedures performed for a patient. The DiagnosticReport results will contain pointers to one or more Observation resources that contain the component results. If you are familiar with HL7v2, DiagnosticReport is analogous to an OBR segment, where Observation is like an OBX segment. For example, consider a CBC (Complete Blood Count) test. The overall CBC test would be represented as a DiagnosticReport resource. The component results (white blood cell count, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelet count, etc.) would each be returned in independent Observation resources. Most systems expect to receive a LOINC code identifying each component. An Observation resource will be returned for a component result even if a LOINC code is not found, however the Observation.code property will be empty. Some labs, such as pathology or cytology, often file a PDF, or a link to a PDF or other document as the result. We do not currently support returning PDF content or other reference pointer content via FHIR, however the test will be discoverable via a DiagnosticReport search. For microbiology labs, the DiagnosticReport resource represents the culture. It includes references to Observation for each isolate. The isolates may then either reference an Observation for each method, or, if there is no method provided by the lab system, then the isolate will reference Observations for each sensitivity result. If methods are provided by the lab, then the method Observations will reference the sensitivity results. The two potential structures are outlined below. Microbiology results without methods: Culture (DiagnosticReport) Isolate A (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Isolate B (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Microbiology results with methods: Culture (DiagnosticReport) Isolate A (Observation) Method 1 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Method 2 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Isolate B (Observation) Method 1 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Method 2 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) The category element is populated with SNOMED codes. In November 2021 and later, these codes are based on a mapping from component records to external SNOMED codes. From August 2021 to May 2021, this applies only to Netherlands environments and these codes are based on the value in the Order Type item in Epic. The following SNOMED codes are supported, and must be mapped in the External Mapping Utility: 252275004-Hematology (Hematologie) 275711006-Chemistry (Klinische chemie) 68793005-Serology (Serologie/ immunologie) 395124008-Virology (Virologie) 314076009-Toxicology (Toxicologie) 19851009-Microbiology (Microbiologie) 405825005-Molecular genetics (Moleculaire genetica)When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. executor_description:
The FHIR Observation resource defines measurements and assertions about a patient, including LDA-W (lines, drains, airways, and wound) data. There are two types of LDA-W data: LDA properties are documented only once. For example, a nurse might insert a line and document properties such as the insertion time, the body site, and the method of insertion. This data is searchable using the FHIR Observation resource and can be filed into Epic. LDA assessments are performed over time. For example, a nurse might inspect an inserted line regularly to make sure the site is clean or assess a wound to see if a new dressing should be applied. This data can be filed into Epic and, starting in the February 2022 version of Epic, is searchable using the R4 version of the FHIR Observation resource. This resource returns only data for patients with active LDAs and wounds. When an LDA-W is completed or otherwise removed from the patient's chart, it will no longer be returned by this API.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. The Observation (Labs) resource returns component level data for lab results. Observation is not normally used on its own to access lab results, because it is limited to reading microbiology sensitivities (method level, isolate level, and sensitivity level) and textual (narrative and impression) Observations. Instead, a system queries the DiagnosticReport resource to identify all lab procedures performed for a patient. The DiagnosticReport results will contain pointers to one or more Observation resources that contain the component results. If you are familiar with HL7v2, DiagnosticReport is analogous to an OBR segment, where Observation is like an OBX segment. For example, consider a CBC (Complete Blood Count) test. The overall CBC test would be represented as a DiagnosticReport resource. The component results (white blood cell count, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelet count, etc.) would each be returned in independent Observation resources. Most systems expect to receive a LOINC code identifying each component. An Observation resource will be returned for a component result even if a LOINC code is not found, however the Observation.code property will be empty. Some labs, such as pathology or cytology, often file a PDF, or a link to a PDF or other document as the result. We do not currently support returning PDF content or other reference pointer content via FHIR, however the test will be discoverable via a DiagnosticReport search. For microbiology labs, the DiagnosticReport resource represents the culture. It includes references to Observation for each isolate. The isolates may then either reference an Observation for each method, or, if there is no method provided by the lab system, then the isolate will reference Observations for each sensitivity result. If methods are provided by the lab, then the method Observations will reference the sensitivity results. The two potential structures are outlined below. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Method 2 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Isolate B (Observation) Method 1 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Method 2 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. The FHIR Observation Social History resource searches for patient observations which include any of the following types of data:
Type of data Epic version Description

Smoking history

November 2019 or later

The status of a patient's tobacco use. This could be used to determine if the patient is a current or former tobacco user, what type of tobacco product is/was used, and the dates the patient started and, if a former user, stopped using tobacco. Starting in Epic version February 2022, this includes passive exposure information in the code response element.

Alcohol use history

November 2021 or later

The patient’s alcohol use history and, if applicable, the type and amount of alcohol the patient consumes.

Drug use history

November 2021 or later

The patient’s drug use history and, if applicable, the type and amount of drugs the patient consumes.

Living situation

November 2021 or later

The patient’s current living situation.

Socioeconomic history

February 2022 or later

The patient’s demographic and employment information.
 Social documentation

February 2022 or later

  The social documentation notes stored in the patient’s history.

The FHIR Observation.Create (Vitals) resource can file to all flowsheet rows, including vital signs. This resource can file vital signs for all flowsheets. When a patient-facing app uses this API, it writes to patient-entered flowsheets. Before that can be done, a user in Epic must place an order to create the episode and patient entered flowsheets that will be filed to. Clinician or backend apps using this API will file to the same flowsheets that clinicians can document in. An error is returned if a reading already exists. If an ID is included in the request, an error is returned. The server assigns an ID to the newly created resource. Alternatives: For patient-entered information, there is an equivalent Incoming HL7v2 Incoming Clinical Documentation Flowsheet Data - Patient Entered Interface. For non-patient-entered information, there is an equivalent Incoming HL7v2 Incoming Clinical Documentation Flowsheet Data Interface. Encounter Considerations: For non-Patient contexts, there are several limitations with this web service compared to the HL7v2 Interface alternative. Cannot write to closed encounters. Cannot write to future appointments. Cannot create an encounter on the fly. Cannot match to an encounter without an Encounter FHIR ID (i.e. fuzzy match). Patient-context Considerations: This service can only file one reading at a time. For patient-entered information, this can trigger multiple notifications to the provider. If this is a concern, consider using the HL7v2 Interface alternative, which can file multiple readings at a time. Try It: An error will be returned if the reading already exists. The FHIR Observation resource defines information about a measurement or simple assertion made about a patient. The FHIR Observation Smoking History resource retrieves the status of a patient's tobacco use. This could be used to determine if the patient is a current or former tobacco user, what type of tobacco product is/was used, and the dates the patient started and, if a former user, stopped using tobacco. The Observation resource corresponds to the following Common Clinical Data Set (CCDS) Elements: Smoking Status The Read interaction enables the look up of an Observation resource by a constant server ID. queryParams.description: Use "obstetrics-gynecology" to search for OB/Gyn history details. Either this or code is required, but both are allowed.
The LOINC code of the observation.

Date range to search for deliveries. All deliveries with an effective date within the specified date range are returned.  Deliveries with no effective date are returned if the search range has no start date (return everything before the specified date). They are not returned if there is a start date but no end date.  Deliveries with fuzzy dates (only a year or month/year), are returned if there is any overlap between the date range and the fuzziness range. For example, if the outcome date is 2009 and the start of the search is 6/5/2009, the 2009 delivery is returned.

Reference to a pregnancy EpisodeOfCare resource. If patient or subject is also provided, they must match the patient attached to the EpisodeOfCare resource. If not provided, observations associated with all pregnancy episodes for the patient are included.
Reference to a patient resource. If both patient and subject are provided, they must match.
The FHIR Patient ID.

The FHIR Observation resource defines measurements and assertions about a patient, including vital signs, laboratory data, imaging results, devices measurements, clinical assessment tools, personal characteristics, social history, and core characteristics. The FHIR Observation Social History resource searches for patient observations which include any of the following types of data:
Type of data Description

Smoking history

The status of a patient's tobacco use. This could be used to determine if the patient is a current or former tobacco user, what type of tobacco product is/was used, and the dates the patient started and, if a former user, stopped using tobacco

Alcohol use history

The patient’s alcohol use history and, if applicable, the type and amount of alcohol the patient consumes.

Drug use history

The patient’s drug use history and, if applicable, the type and amount of drugs the patient consumes.

Living situation

The patient’s current living situation.

executor_description:
The Observation (Labs) resource represents component level data for lab results. Observation is limited to reading microbiology sensitivities (method level, isolate level, and sensitivity level), lab component results, and textual (narrative and impression) Observations. To identify all lab procedures performed for a patient, a client might consider using the DiagnosticReport resource instead, which will contain pointers to one or more Observation resources that contain the component results. If you are familiar with HL7v2, DiagnosticReport is analogous to an OBR segment, where Observation is like an OBX segment. For example, consider a CBC (Complete Blood Count) test. The overall CBC test would be represented as a DiagnosticReport resource. The component results (white blood cell count, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelet count, etc.) would each be returned in independent Observation resources. The $lastn interaction shares much with the standard Search interaction, but serves a more specific function by returning the most recent lab results of a particular category for a patient. For example, if the category is hematology, the $lastn operation will return each of the most recent lab results for hematology, such as the most recent white blood cell count, the most recent hemoglobin count, the most recent platelet count, and so on. This is distinct from using the Search interaction in that $lastn will return the most recent results from each subtype of a category, whereas a Search interaction returns all of the hematology results ever recorded for a patient that meet the specified search parameters, including historical results that might be superseded by more recent results. $lastn supports searching only by certain SNOMED code categories. Result components in Epic must be mapped to one of the supported SNOMED codes in order to be returned as part of a $lastn response. If a client wants to search on a specific result component ID or LOINC code, the client should instead use the Search interaction, which supports code as a search parameter. executor_description:
The Observation (Labs) resource returns component level data for lab results. Observation is not normally used on its own to access lab results, because it is limited to reading microbiology sensitivities (method level, isolate level, and sensitivity level) and textual (narrative and impression) Observations. Instead, a system queries the DiagnosticReport resource to identify all lab procedures performed for a patient. The DiagnosticReport results will contain pointers to one or more Observation resources that contain the component results. If you are familiar with HL7v2, DiagnosticReport is analogous to an OBR segment, where Observation is like an OBX segment. For example, consider a CBC (Complete Blood Count) test. The overall CBC test would be represented as a DiagnosticReport resource. The component results (white blood cell count, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelet count, etc.) would each be returned in independent Observation resources. Most systems expect to receive a LOINC code identifying each component. An Observation resource will be returned for a component result even if a LOINC code is not found, however the Observation.code property will be empty. Some labs, such as pathology or cytology, often file a PDF, or a link to a PDF or other document as the result. We do not currently support returning PDF content or other reference pointer content via FHIR, however the test will be discoverable via a DiagnosticReport search. For microbiology labs, the DiagnosticReport resource represents the culture. It includes references to Observation for each isolate. The isolates may then either reference an Observation for each method, or, if there is no method provided by the lab system, then the isolate will reference Observations for each sensitivity result. If methods are provided by the lab, then the method Observations will reference the sensitivity results. The two potential structures are outlined below. Microbiology results without methods: Culture (DiagnosticReport) Isolate A (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Isolate B (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Microbiology results with methods: Culture (DiagnosticReport) Isolate A (Observation) Method 1 (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) b. Image and hierarchy datatypes are not returned. The SmartData element value is the unique SmartData identifier for the SmartData element.

The Observation (Labs) resource returns component level data for lab results. Observation is not normally used on its own to access lab results, because it is limited to reading microbiology sensitivities (method level, isolate level, and sensitivity level) and textual (narrative and impression) Observations. Instead, a system queries the DiagnosticReport resource to identify all lab procedures performed for a patient. The DiagnosticReport results will contain pointers to one or more Observation resources that contain the component results. If you are familiar with HL7v2, DiagnosticReport is analogous to an OBR segment, where Observation is like an OBX segment. For example, consider a CBC (Complete Blood Count) test. The overall CBC test would be represented as a DiagnosticReport resource. The component results (white blood cell count, red blood cell count, hemoglobin, platelet count, etc.) would each be returned in independent Observation resources. Most systems expect to receive a LOINC code identifying each component. An Observation resource will be returned for a component result even if a LOINC code is not found, however the Observation.code property will be empty. Some labs, such as pathology or cytology, often file a PDF, or a link to a PDF or other document as the result. We do not currently support returning PDF content or other reference pointer content via FHIR, however the test will be discoverable via a DiagnosticReport search. For microbiology labs, the DiagnosticReport resource represents the culture. It includes references to Observation for each isolate. The isolates may then either reference an Observation for each method, or, if there is no method provided by the lab system, then the isolate will reference Observations for each sensitivity result. If methods are provided by the lab, then the method Observations will reference the sensitivity results. The two potential structures are outlined below. Microbiology results without methods: Culture (DiagnosticReport) Isolate A (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Isolate B (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic W (Observation) Sensitivity results for antibiotic X (Observation) Microbiology results with methods: Culture (DiagnosticReport) Isolate A (Observation) Method 1 (Observation) a. The FHIR Procedure resource defines an activity performed on or with a patient as part of the provision of care. It corresponds with surgeries and procedures performed, including endoscopies and biopsies, as well as less invasive actions like counseling and physiotherapy. The Procedure (Surgeries) API is designed to summarize any performed surgical procedures for a patient. Other types of procedures may be returned in other APIs, such as the Procedure (Orders) API for procedures created from orders. Organizations can have differences when determining which performable activities are classified as procedures, so the types of activities included in FHIR Procedure search can vary between organizations. Because terminology codes for procedures are often billing related, some procedures might not have a standard code (for example, CPT), especially when billing activities are not performed within Epic. For organizations that do perform billing activities within Epic, procedures might not have a CPT code until the charges are generated for the procedure. This resource is designed for a high-level summarization around the occurrence of a procedure, and not for specific procedure log documentation - a concept that does not yet have a defined FHIR Resource. When searching, only completed procedures are returned. To gather a complete list of surgical procedure information for a patient , three different Procedure APIs must be consulted. While a surgical procedure may be documented in multiple places in Epic, it will be returned only by one Procedure FHIR API, in the following order of precedence: Procedure (Orders): Includes any procedure that is ordered by a clinician and completed during an encounter. If a procedure is returned by this API, it won’t be returned by the Procedure (Surgeries) or Procedure (Surgical History) APIs. Procedure (Surgeries): Includes surgical procedures attached to a surgical log. If a procedure is returned by this API, it won’t be returned by the Procedure (Surgical History) API. Procedure (Surgical History): Includes any manually documented surgical history or pertinent negatives that were not documented on a surgical log or ordered within Epic.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. The FHIR Procedure resource defines an activity performed on or with a patient as part of the provision of care. It corresponds with surgeries and procedures performed, including endoscopies and biopsies, as well as less invasive actions like counseling and physiotherapy. Note: The STU3 version of this web service currently supports only order procedure records. Dental and surgica procedures are not yet supported. You can use the Procedure.Read (DSTU2) web service if you need to support dental or surgical procedures. This resource is designed for a high-level summarization around the occurrence of a procedure, and not for specific procedure log documentation - a concept that does not yet have a defined FHIR Resource. When searching, only completed procedures are returned. The read interaction enables the lookup of a Procedure resource by a constant server ID. The read interaction allows clients to store only the server ID, and with a single request, retrieve the most up-to-date information about a procedure. Read interactions typically begin with a client having previously established a relationship, often through querying for Procedures through the search interaction. The FHIR Procedure resource defines an activity performed on or with a patient as part of the provision of care. It corresponds with surgeries and procedures performed, including endoscopies and biopsies, as well as less invasive actions like counseling and physiotherapy. Because terminology codes for procedures are often billing related, some procedures might not have a terminology code, especially when billing activities are not performed within Epic. The Procedure (Surgeries) API is designed to summarize any performed surgical procedures for a patient. Other types of procedures may be returned in other APIs, such as the Procedure (Orders) API for procedures created from orders. This resource is designed for a high-level summarization around the occurrence of a procedure, and not for specific procedure log documentation - a concept that does not yet have a defined FHIR Resource. The read interaction enables the lookup of a Procedure resource by a constant server ID. It corresponds with surgeries and procedures performed, including endoscopies and biopsies, as well as less invasive actions like counseling and physiotherapy. The Procedure (Surgical History) API is designed to summarize historical surgical procedures a patient has had, as well as pertinent negatives (indicating a patient has not had a particular surgery). Other types of procedures may be returned in other APIs, such as the Procedure (Orders) API for procedures created from orders. In Epic version May 2021 and earlier, be aware when using the Procedure resource that each unique procedure could appear twice for patients because it can appear as both a Surgical History entry and a Surgical Procedure entry. To gather a complete list of surgical procedure information for a patient , three different Procedure APIs must be consulted. While a surgical procedure may be documented in multiple places in Epic, it will be returned only by one Procedure FHIR API, in the following order of precedence: Procedure (Orders): Includes any procedure that is ordered by a clinician and completed during an encounter. If a procedure is returned by this API, it won’t be returned by the Procedure (Surgeries) or Procedure (Surgical History) APIs. Procedure (Surgeries): Includes surgical procedures attached to a surgical log. If a procedure is returned by this API, it won’t be returned by the Procedure (Surgical History) API. The $match operation accepts a set of patient demographic information and attempts to find a single high-confidence match for a patient record in the target organization’s system. Epic’s implementation of this operation requires that the onlyCertainMatches parameter be set to “true”. This means that the operation returns a matching Patient resource only if one high-confidence match is found. When more than one patient record in the target system is matched with high confidence, or when no patient can be matched with high confidence to the provided demographics, this operation returns no results and a corresponding error: Multiple high-confidence matches: OperationOutcome code 59011 (“The matching operation found multiple potential matches, but requires only one match.”) No high-confidence matches, but one or more low-confidence matches: OperationOutcome code 59013 (“The matching operation found one or more possible matches, but did not find a certain match.”) No high-confidence or low-confidence matches: OperationOutcome 4101 (“Resource request returns no results.”) When a single high-confidence match has been found, this resource returns the matching FHIR R4 Patient resource in a Bundle structure. In most cases all of the following information is required to match to a patient record with high confidence: Exact patient name Patient birthdate One or more of the following: The patient EPI identifier An Identity ID type (IIT) identifier for the patient The patient SSN Patient address Patient phone number This functionality may require a greater minimum data set than listed above depending on the security policies and custom logic in place at an organization. The above is only the minimum data set required to match a patient with this API. A user or staff member accessing this FHIR resource must have appropriate security to have search details, demographic details, and/or PCP details included in the Patient resource. Additionally, if an Epic organization has configured service area restrictions, the user accessing this FHIR resource must be authorized to view patients in the target service area. This operation is not supported for MyChart users. The Patient.$match operation is similar to Patient.Search (R4). For systems that need a single high confidence match, Epic recommends using Patient.$match instead of Patient.Search. An example would be a back-end system without an end user. executor_description:
This web service allows filtering or searching for patients based on a number of parameters, and retrieves patient demographic information from a patient's chart for each matching patient record. This service also does not respect the same filtering as MyChart, with the exception of the careProvider parameter. A user or staff member accessing this FHIR resource must have appropriate security to have search details, demographic details, and/or PCP details included in the Patient resource. A MyChart user accessing this FHIR resource must be authorized to view patient information in MyChart. Additionally, this FHIR resource returns patient identifiers only to MyChart users with security to see patient IDs. If an Epic organization has configured service area restrictions, the user accessing this FHIR resource must also be authorized to view patients in the target service area.

Starting in Epic Version

New Features or Changes to Patient.Search (R4)

November 2022

A new operation, Patient.$match (R4), has been released. Epic now recommends using Patient.$match for most patient-searching use cases, because it is designed to find specific patients with high confidence.

May 2022 (February 2022 and November 2021 by special update)

Including patient search parameters in R4 FHIR is now optional to make a request in a patient-facing context when using OAuth 2.0 authorization for the patient on whose behalf authorization to the system was granted.

November 2021 (August 2021 by special update)

Patient.Search requests can now use a patient identifier without specifying the ID Type. This includes FHIR IDs, SSNs, EPT IDs, and more. We still recommend including IDType for performance reasons.

August 2021

Epic organizations can allow more flexibility in the search parameters by enabling filter-based searching. Patients must match on all criteria to be returned by the search, but Epic organizations can configure a specified amount of variance in the patient's demographics that still return a match.

May 2019

Patient.Search requests require one of the following minimum data sets by default in order to match and return a patient record:

  • FHIR ID
  • {IDType}|{ID}
  • SSN identifier
  • Given name, family name, and birthdate
  • Given name, family name, legal sex, and phone number/email

This functionality may require a greater minimum data set than that you've tested with depending on the security policies and custom logic in place at an organization. The above is only the minimum data set required to match a patient with this API.

Note that the ID type for the MRN may not be "MRN" at every customer.

FHIR Errors come in two flavors: Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

The Patient.Create web service creates a new patient record or returns an existing one: If a single high-threshold match is found in the target environment based on Identity IDs or demographics, the service returns the existing patient. If multiple high-threshold matches are found in the target environment based on Identity IDs or demographics, the service returns a 400 Bad Request. If a match is found in external EMPI, the service creates a shell patient in the target environment and returns it. If no match is found, a single low-threshold match is found, or multiple low-threshold matches are found, the service creates a net new patient in the target environment.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. FHIR Errors come in two flavors: Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

executor_description:
The FHIR MedicationStatement resource defines detailed information about medications being consumed by a patient. The medication information may come from e.g. the patient's memory, from a prescription bottle, or from a list of medications the patient, clinician or other party maintains and therefore can be less specific than the MedicationOrder resource. The MedicationStatement resource is a high-level summary of medications being used, reported by patients or care providers. It is not a listing of specific prescriptions or administrations, which instead are available in the MedicationOrder and MedicationAdministration resources, respectively. The Read interaction enables the look up of a MedicationStatement resource by a constant server ID. Clients can store only the server ID, and with a single request, retrieve the most up-to-date information about the MedicationStatement. executor_description:
The MedicationStatement resource represents all medications a patient is taking, be it those ordered in the EMR or reported externally by either another organization or the patient themselves. The medicationStatement resource information reflects the details about how the patient is actually taking the medication even if it differs from what was ordered. The search interaction enables you to query for medication orders based on a patient and optionally status or category. You can use the Patient Search endpoint to establish an identifier for a patient without previously receiving unique identification from the server for the patient. Starting in February 2022 or November 2021 by special update, organizations in the Netherlands can use this resource to satisfy the requirements of the MedicationUse profile. Consider the following chart when determining what resource to use when identifying medications a patient is taking. When creating a new application, it is recommended to use the latest FHIR version available.
Resource Inpatient Orders? Outpatient Orders? Patient Reported Medications?
MedicationOrder (DSTU2) Yes Yes No
MedicationStatement (DSTU2) Yes Yes Yes
MedicationRequest (STU3) Yes Yes No
MedicationStatement (STU3) Yes Yes Yes
MedicationRequest (Orders) (R4) Yes Yes Yes

queryParams.description: The category of medication orders to search for. By default all categories are searched.  Supported categories:  inpatient outpatient community patientspecified

The date when the patient was taking the medication. This parameter corresponds to the MedicationStatement.effectivePeriod element. Medication orders that do not have start and end dates within the search parameter dates are filtered. If the environment supports multiple time zones, the search dates are adjusted one day in both directions, so more medications might be returned than expected. Use caution when filtering a medication list by effective date as it is possible to filter out important active medications. Starting in the November 2022 version of Epic, this parameter is respected. In May 2022 and earlier versions of Epic, this parameter is allowed, but is ignored and no date filtering is applied.
The FHIR Patient ID. Either this element or Subject is required.

The status for medication orders. By default, active is assumed. Active must be present in all searches (you cannot search for just completed meds). In the Netherlands, all statuses are returned by default and active does not have to be present in all searches. Supported statuses:  on-hold completed stopped active
The FHIR patient ID. Either this element or Patient is required.

Either the patient, subject, or encounter must be provided.
Reference to an Encounter resource the procedure request is in.

If “true”, only scannable orders and procedures are returned in the response. This feature requires a user to have login department context as part of the API request, otherwise error code 59100 is returned.
Reference to a patient resource for which the request is ordered.
Reference to a practitioner resource who is the authorizing provider for the procedure request.
The status of the request. Supported values include:  draft active completed revoked unknown This service returns all statuses if this element is not specified.
Reference to a patient resource for which the request is ordered.

queryParams.description: Points a search to the correct subresource. Specify “http://snomed.info/sct%7C738906000” for ServiceRequest. Data will be returned if this parameter is left blank, or if one of its values is the dental category.

If “true”, only scannable orders and procedures are returned in the response. This feature requires a user to have login department context as part of the API request, otherwise error code 59100 is returned
The patient to search for data for.

The procedure statuses to search for. This parameter is ignored if the “_id” parameter is included in the search. The accepted values are active, draft, completed, and revoked, which respectively correspond to the Planned, Planning, Completed, and Discontinued statuses of procedures. If the status property is not set, procedures of every status (including Draft and Discontinued) will be returned. If set, only the specified status will be returned.

These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

queryParams.description: Search for Practitioner resources by any part of an address, such as street or city, where a practitioner can be found.
Search for Practitioner resources using the city portion of the address at which the practitioner can be found. This parameter must be used with the address_postalcode parameter.
Search for Practitioner resources using the postal code portion of the address at which the practitioner can be found.
Search for Practitioner resources using the state portion of the address at which the practitioner can be found.
Search for Practitioner resources by family (last) name. Family name searching supports both exact and "sounds like" matches.  Either Family or Specialty is required for a search to succeed.
Search for Practitioner resources using the following gender codes: "female", "male", or "unknown".
Search for Practitioner resources by given (first) name. Given name searching supports both exact and "sounds like" matches.
Search for Practitioner resources by specialty in the format [code system]|[code].  Either Family or Specialty is required for a search to succeed.

The city specified in the address. City cannot be specified without state or ZIP code.
A ZIP code specified in the address.
A state specified in the address.
A portion of the family name. If name or identifier is provided, this is not required.
A portion of the given name. If Given is provided, Family must also be provided.

A practitioner's identifier, such as NPI. If Family or Name is provided, this is not required.  Starting in November 2018, this web service supports using ID and ID type combinations, such as Practitioner?identifier=External|802559.

The FHIR RelatedPerson resource is typically an entity with a personal or professional relationship to the patient. RelatedPersons are often a source of information about the patient. For integrations with Epic, the RelatedPerson is represented by a MyChart account record ID and their link to a Patient record ID. Typically the RelatedPerson represents a MyChart proxy for the patient. The read interaction enables the lookup of a RelatedPerson resource by a constant server ID. The read interaction allows clients to store only the server ID, and with a single request, retrieve the most up-to-date information about the resource. Read interactions typically begin with a client having previously established a relationship. In this case, clients will get the FHIR ID from an OpenID Connect (OIDC) workflow.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. The ValueSet resource represents a subset of the codes in a code system that is supported by a given server. The $expand operation of the ValueSet resource can be used by a FHIR API consumer to determine: What values to expect back from the server as a result of a Read or Search operation. What values they can pass in to the server when performing a Create or Update operation. The $expand operation response represents a single ValueSet resource. Epic currently supports querying the ValueSet.$expand operation with search parameters. For example, a client may perform a query in the format /ValueSet/$expand?parameter=value. Epic does not support querying the ValueSet.$expand operation for a specific identifier (/ValueSet/[id]/$expand). The following resources are currently supported for use with the ValueSet.$expand operation. Additional resources will be supported in future versions.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. FHIR Errors come in two flavors: Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

Specifies the direction of the interaction with regards to the ValueSet. Options include "outgoing" or "incoming".  outgoing - for query parameters and response content incoming - for incoming POST/PUT body

A filter string used to further refine the ValueSet context to a specific sub-resource based on the resource's category element, and in some cases, additional details.  Example: filter=category:document-information,workflow:registration, level:encounter,resource:ej5R7X.4RdaFNR5vWdsTpVTtccmkRkWJcKixc5XVY4cQ3 Epic currently supports the following filters:  category:clinical-note category:document-information The following additional filters can be combined with category:document-information to further refine results:  workflow:general workflow:registration level:patient level:encounter level:order resource:<patient FHIR ID> resource:<encounter FHIR ID>

executor_description:
The AllergyIntolerance resource defines clinical information about a patient's allergic response to a substance. It defines the substance that elicited the response, as well as when the reaction occurred, the severity, and the type of reaction noted. The AllergyIntolerance resource can also accommodate search by ID and by patient, allowing it to return a list of allergies. If a patient has no active allergies, an AllergyIntolerance resource will be returned indicating whether the patient's allergies have never been reviewed (are not on file), or if they have been reviewed and it has been determined that they have no known allergies. This resource can also return unconfirmed AllergyIntolerance resources in the "holding tank" that drives the EpicCare Reconcile Outside Data Activity. Note - once a clinician reconciles an allergy, a new AllergyIntolerance resource associated with the reconciled allergy will be available in the normal AllergyIntolerance.Search results, and the unconfirmed AllergyIntolerance in the "holding tank" will no longer appear in the AllergyIntolerance.Search results. The allergen name and codes.
Refers to the risk of clinical harm of a reaction to the substance.
The AllergyIntolerance FHIR ID.
Any comments associated with the allergy.
If an allergy has a noted date or a resolved date, those dates are specified here.
Reference to a patient resource for whom the allergy is relevant.
List of known reactions the patient had to the substance.
If the allergy is on the patient's chart, this element specifies "confirmed". If it is a newly created allergy and and still needs to be reconciled, it is "unconfirmed".
The date the allergy was recorded in Epic.
The document metadata.

The Binary.Read (Handoff) web service returns content associated with a handoff report. Typically, a client obtains the Binary ID by first completing a DocumentReference (Handoff) read or search interaction. Handoff reports allow clinicians to communicate important time-sensitive information between shifts. Handoff reports are specialty-specific, so clinicians write and review reports that contain only information relevant to the services they perform. Each handoff report is split into several fields, each of which is associated with a particular purpose, such as “To Do” or “Medications.” One DocumentReference handoff entity represents a single handoff report field for a single specialty. The text of each field is contained in a separate Binary (Handoff) resource response. This Epic implementation of Binary supports retrieving Clinical Document Architecture (CDA) documents via this FHIR resource. Note that Binary does not return existing CDA documents for a patient. Instead, it generates new CDA documents based on the current clinical content in the system. This prevents communicating stale data and ensures that the CDA content contains only data that the requesting user is authorized to view. The Binary read interaction enables the look up of a binary resource by a constant server ID. The read interaction allows clients to store only the server ID, and with a single request, retrieve the most up-to-date binary content. Read interactions typically begin with a client having previously established a relationship, often through querying for DocumentReference resources through the search interaction. Note that because a new CDA document might be generated for each new request, it is not safe to assume that DocumentReference will always return the same Binary ID for the most recently generated document, as new Binary IDs might be generated if there is new clinical content available, which will generate a new CDA document. You likely want to work with the CDA documents rather than a FHIR resource. Therefore, when making a read request, we recommend that you do not explicitly specify FHIR content types such as "application/xml+fhir" or "application/json+fhir" in the Accept header. When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. FHIR Errors come in two flavors: Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

executor_description:
The FHIR Appointment $book operation schedules an appointment that was returned by the $find operation. It will take a patient ID, appointment FHIR ID from the result selected from the $find results, and optionally a free-text note to store with the appointment. A typical workflow would involve an end user, who is intending to book an appointment for patient, entering in some basic criteria, such as when the appointment would occur, what specialty or visit type is desired, and optional information about the patient, such as date of birth, sex, or any provider preferences the patient has.  The user app would then collect those criteria and submit them using the $find operation.  The scheduling system would use organization-defined rules to identify potential appointments slots, and returns those for the user to review.  The user would review the possible options, and in collaboration with the patient, select the best option.  For new patients, the app would perform a Patient.Create interaction.  The app would then book the appointment using the $book operation. It includes links to the Condition resource (the patient's long term Problem List) and the Goal resource (the patient's longitudinal goals) as well as in-line detail about upcoming appointments, referral orders, and upcoming orders. executor_description:
The FHIR CarePlan resource is a broad container for summarizing the plan of treatment for a patient. It includes links to the Condition resource (the patient's long term Problem List) and the Goal resource (the patient's longitudinal goals) as well as in-line detail about upcoming appointments, referral orders, and upcoming orders. The CarePlan resource is designed for provider planning and documentation, not patient interaction. This resource is also designed for stating specific activities related to a single patient, rather than generic protocols for condition treatment (a Protocol resource will be defined in a later version of FHIR). By default, only the patient's longitudinal CarePlan is returned. However, encounter-level CarePlans can also be requested. These encounter-level CarePlans include narrative content, such as patient instructions, and assassment and plan of treatment notes that are not associated with any particular condition. The CarePlan resource corresponds to the following Common Clinical Data Set (CCDS) Elements: Assessment and Plan of Treatment. The Search interaction enables the client to query for the care plan for a given patient. queryParams.description: Limits the search to a particular organ location. Format: “http://snomed.info/sct|SNOMEDCODE” where SNOMEDCODE is the numeric portion of the code associated with a particular body structure. For example, enter “http://snomed.info/sct|18639004” to search for left kidney structures. May send multiple entries separated by commas.

Limits the search to all organs, or to specifically donor or recipient organs. Enter “organs” for all organs, “http://snomed.info/sct|91723000” for donor organs, or “http://snomed.info/sct|280115004” for recipient organs.
The patient for which to perform the search.

queryParams.description: Accepts a string for a specific tooth in the patient’s mouth. Format: “[Notation OID]|[tooth ID]”, where “Notation OID” is the OID matching the tooth notation system used to communicate the tooth ID. May send multiple entries separated by commas. Supported notations are Universal (94010), FDI (94011) and Palmer (94013). Ex. “urn:oid:1.2.840.114350.1.13.861.1.7.3.866976.94010|32”
Points a search to the correct subresource of tooth. Either “teeth” or “302214001” are accepted. These values are functionally equivalent.

This web service adds problems to a patient's problem list. A clinician must reconcile the problem in Epic before it is officially accepted into the patient Chart. executor_description:
The FHIR Condition resource defines detailed information about a Condition, problem, or diagnosis relevant to the health of the patient. Conditions are typically associated with other resources, such as the reason for a prescription, procedure, diagnostic test, etc. A Condition might be acute or chronic, but it is not used to represent an adverse reaction or an allergy intolerance. The Condition resource corresponds to the following Common Clinical Data Set (CCDS) Elements: Problems and Health Concerns. The Search interaction enables the client to query for all problems associated with a given patient's Conditions. The client, having established the patient in question, now wishes to retrieve the list of that patient's problems or documented health concerns. Note that this resource retrieves only data stored in problem list records. As a result, medical history data documented outside of a patient's problem list isn't available to applications using this service unless that data is retrieved using another method.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Conditions are typically associated with other resources, such as the reason for a prescription, procedure, diagnostic test, etc. A Condition might be acute or chronic, but it is not used to represent an adverse reaction or an allergy intolerance. The Condition resource corresponds to the following Common Clinical Data Set (CCDS) Elements: Problems and Health Concerns. The Read interaction enables the look up of a Condition resource by a constant server ID. This web service retrieves problem list and health status data from a patient's chart. This includes any data found in the patient chart across all encounters. executor_description:
This web service retrieves problem list and health status data from a patient's chart. This includes any data found in the patient chart across all encounters. Note that very few Epic organizations record a health status for patients, so in most cases this resource will be used to retrieve problem list items only. This resource can be queried by a combination of patient ID and status. This resource returns a smaller subset of elements for health status conditions as compared to problem list items. For health status, severity, onsetPeriod, abatementPeriod, and note elements are not populated. Some problems on the problem list may be marked with a class of "Health Concern", indicating that the problem is of special concern. Problems flagged with this special class will be returned alongside the other problems, however they will be annotated with a special category of health-concern. Note that this resource retrieves only data stored in problem list (LPL) records. As a result, medical history data documented outside of a patient's problem list isn't available to applications using this service unless that data is retrieved using another method. A user or staff member accessing this FHIR resource must have appropriate security to view problem list items and/or health status. MyChart users must have security to see problem list information. Patient-level break-the-glass functionality is in place for this resource.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. This web service is designed for scanning integrations to be used only with Epic's Managed Care product. The Hyperdrive client can be configured to launch an external scan acquisition application that allows users to acquire scanned documents through a Document Management System (DMS) and associate documents with Epic records. Currently we support associating documents acquired in this manner only with Employer Group records, which represent groups of members using the same benefit plan, and Account records, which group together employer groups for the purposes of generating invoices and receiving payments. Contextual information, like a FHIR Group ID representing an Employer Group or an Account ID representing an Account, can be passed as a context variable as part of the launch workflow. The scanning software can then use the Group.Read (Employer Group) or Account.Read (Premium Billing) API to access information about the Employer Group or Account. executor_description:
The FHIR DocumentReference resource describes information about a document, the associated patient and author, and information about its creation. The DocumentReference resource only contains metadata about the document. The actual document content is accessed via the Binary resource that is referenced in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.url property. Note that DocumentReference does not return existing CDA documents for a patient. Instead, it generates new CDA documents based on the current clinical content in the system. This prevents communicating stale data, and also ensures that the CDA content only contains data that the requesting user is authorized to view. Note: Only 80 DocumentReference (Generated CCDAs) searches can be made for a given patient in one day. Apps must be prepared to gracefully handle this cap, especially if they will be requesting information multiple times in a day. An app that repeats API calls instead of caching results is more likely to reach the cap. Similar Resources: DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (DSTU2) - Generates a CDA document based on current clinical content in the system. DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (R4) - Functionally the same as DSTU2 with improvements to document generation limit. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (STU3) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. Can only query Epic payer systems. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (R4) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. Can query Epic provider systems.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. The FHIR DocumentReference resource describes information about a document, the associated patient and author, and information about its creation. The DocumentReference resource only contains metadata about the document. The actual document content is accessed via the Binary resource that is referenced in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.url property. Note that DocumentReference does not return existing CDA documents for a patient. Instead, it generates new CDA documents based on the current clinical content in the system. This prevents communicating stale data, and also ensures that the CDA content only contains data that the requesting user is authorized to view. *Note - only 80 CCDA API calls can be made for a patient per day. If an app will be generating CCDAs for each patient encounter, the app should gracefully handle this cap as patients with many encounters are likely to hit the cap or if an app doesn't cache and can repeat making these API calls. Similar Resources: DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (DSTU2) - Generates a CDA document based on current clinical content in the system. DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (R4) - Functionally the same as DSTU2 with improvements to document generation limit. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (STU3) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. Can only query Epic payer systems. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (R4) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. Can query Epic provider systems.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. executor_description:
This web service is designed for scanning integrations to be used only with Epic’s Tapestry module. The Hyperdrive client can be configured to launch an external scan acquisition application that allows users to acquire scanned documents through a Document Management System (DMS) and associate documents with Epic records. Currently we support associating documents in this manner only with Employer Group records, which represent groups of members using the same benefit plan, and Account records, which group together employer groups for the purposes of generating invoices and receiving payments. Contextual information, like a FHIR Group ID representing an Employer Group or an Account ID representing an Account, can be passed as a context variable as part of the launch workflow. The scanning software can then use the Group.Read (Employer Group) or Account.Read (Premium Billing) API to access information about the Employer Group or Account. When the scanning workflow is completed within the scanning system, the scanning application stores the scanned document’s binary data to its server and files metadata about the scan to Epic using the DocumentReference.Create (Non-Patient Document Information) API. For Employer Group and Account scanning workflows, the FHIR Group ID or Account ID provided as a launch context variable must be included in the DocumentReference.context.related property in the DocumentReference.Create (Non-Patient Document Information) API to link the scan to the Employer Group or Account. This API currently supports only the _id search parameter. As a result, it functions similarly to DocumentReference.Read (Non-Patient Document Information) (R4).When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. The DocumentReference handoff API can retrieve the handoff reports for an encounter. Handoff reports allow clinicians to communicate important time-sensitive information between shifts. Handoff reports are specialty-specific, so clinicians write and review reports that contain only information relevant to the services they perform. Each handoff report is split into several fields, and each of those fields is associated with a particular purpose, such as “To Do” or “Medications.” One DocumentReference handoff entity represents a single handoff report field for a single specialty. The text of each field is contained in a separate Binary handoff subresource. The FHIR DocumentReference resource describes information about a document. The DocumentReference resource includes information about a document, the associated patient and author, and information about its creation. The DocumentReference resource only contains metadata about the document. The actual document content is accessed via the Binary resource that is referenced in DocumentReference.content.attachment.url. The DocumentReference resource returns available data for all of the data categories of the Common Clinical Data Set (CCDS). The read interaction enables the lookup of a DocumentReference resource by a constant server ID. Discharge Documentation (18842-5) Consultation (11488-4) History & Physical (34117-2) Progress Note (11506-3) Procedure Note (28570-0) Emergency Department Note (34111-5) Nurse Note (34746-8) Starting in the May 2022 version of Epic or the February 2022 version of Epic by special update:  Discharge Instructions (74213-0) Risk assessment and screening note (75492-9) Note category IDs can also be specified, and correspond to note types in Epic. For the App Orchard sandbox it is '0' "environment type" is '2' for a production instance, '3' for a non-production instance, and '1' for the App Orchard sandbox. The DocumentReference handoff API can retrieve the handoff reports for an encounter. Handoff reports allow clinicians to communicate important time-sensitive information between shifts. Handoff reports are specialty-specific, so clinicians write and review reports that contain only information relevant to the services they perform. Each handoff report is split into several fields, and each of those fields is associated with a particular purpose, such as “To Do” or “Medications.” One DocumentReference handoff entity represents a single handoff report field for a single specialty. The text of each field is contained in a separate Binary handoff subresource.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. The FHIR DocumentReference resource is a resource that can be used to represent many different types of documents. The FHIR DocumentReference (External CCDA) implementation is used to communicate information about a structured C-CDA (Consolidated-Clinical Document Architecture) document that was received from an external source. C-CDA is an HL7 standard for documents used to exchange clinical data between organizations using EHRs. The search interaction enables the client to query for C-CDA document records based on a patient and optionally a date of service or date of document creation/update. Similar Resources: DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (DSTU2) - Generates a CDA document based on current clinical content in the system. DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (R4) - Functionally the same as DSTU2 with improvements to document generation limit. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (STU3) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. Can only query Epic payer systems. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (R4) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. This web service is designed for scanning integrations to be used only with Epic's Managed Care product. The Hyperdrive client can be configured to launch an external scan acquisition application that allows users to acquire scanned documents through a Document Management System (DMS) and associate documents with Epic records. Currently we support associating documents acquired in this manner only with Employer Group records, which represent groups of members using the same benefit plan, and Account records, which group together employer groups for the purposes of generating invoices and receiving payments. Contextual information, like a FHIR Group ID representing an Employer Group or an Account ID representing an Account, can be passed as a context variable as part of the launch workflow. The scanning software can then use the Group.Read (Employer Group) or Account.Read (Premium Billing) API to access information about the Employer Group or Account. When the scanning workflow is completed within the scanning system, the scanning application stores the scanned document’s binary data to its server and files metadata about the scan to Epic using the DocumentReference.Create (Non-Patient Document Information) API. For Employer Group and Account scanning workflows, the FHIR Group ID or Account ID provided as a launch context variable must be included in the DocumentReference.context.related property in the DocumentReference.Create (Non-Patient Document Information) API to link the scan to the Employer Group or Account.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. FHIR Errors come in two flavors: Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

executor_description:
The FHIR DocumentReference resource describes information about a document, the associated patient and author, and information about its creation. The DocumentReference resource only contains metadata about the document. The actual document content is accessed via the Binary resource that is referenced in the DocumentReference.content.attachment.url property. Note that DocumentReference does not return existing CDA documents for a patient. Instead, it generates new CDA documents based on the current clinical content in the system. This prevents communicating stale data, and also ensures that the CDA content only contains data that the requesting user is authorized to view. Similar Resources: DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (DSTU2) - Generates a CDA document based on current clinical content in the system. DocumentReference (Generated CCDA) (R4) - Functionally the same as DSTU2 with improvements to document generation limit. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (STU3) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic. Can only query Epic payer systems. DocumentReference (External CCDA Document) (R4) - Returns external CDA documents received in Epic.
