queryParams.description: Refine a search for DocumentReference resources by passing a LOINC code for document class (CCD and encounter supported). The default LOINC code for CCD is 34133-9 - Summarization of Episode Note. The default LOINC code for Encounter is 11506-3 - Subsequent Evaluation Note.
Search for DocumentReference resources for a specified patient ID.

Refine a search for DocumentReference resources by specifying a date or date range for the DocumentReference content. Enter dates in ISO 8601 format (YYYY[-MM[-DD[THH:MM[:SS][TZ]]]]). Local server time is assumed if time zone information is not included. Common FHIR operators such as gt, lt, ge, le, =, and ap are supported. When no period is specified, a customer setting is used to determine how far to look back. There is also a setting capping lookback. Another setting can limit what encounter types are returned. Encounters without clinical data will not be returned.
Search for DocumentReference resources for a specified patient ID.

executor_description:
The DocumentReference handoff API can retrieve the handoff reports for an encounter. Handoff reports allow clinicians to communicate important time-sensitive information between shifts. Handoff reports are specialty-specific, so clinicians write and review reports that contain only information relevant to the services they perform. Each handoff report is split into several fields, and each of those fields is associated with a particular purpose, such as “To Do” or “Medications.” One DocumentReference handoff entity represents a single handoff report field for a single specialty. The text of each field is contained in a separate Binary handoff subresource. The note category ID or the LOINC code for the document type.  code= By default, we support the following LOINC codes for document type. Epic organizations can support additional LOINC codes beyond these defaults with custom mapping. Discharge Documentation (18842-5) Consultation (11488-4) History & Physical (34117-2) Progress Note (11506-3) Procedure Note (28570-0) Emergency Department Note (34111-5) Nurse Note (34746-8) Starting in the May 2022 version of Epic or the February 2022 version of Epic by special update:  Discharge Instructions (74213-0) Risk assessment and screening note (75492-9) Note category IDs can also be specified, and correspond to note types in Epic. The format for using Note category IDs is: type=system|code, where: system="1.2.840.114350.1.13.[environment identifier].[environment_type].7.4.737880.5010" code=the note category ID "environment identifier" is different per epic instance and should be determined at time of implementation. For the App Orchard sandbox it is '0' "environment type" is '2' for a production instance, '3' for a non-production instance, and '1' for the App Orchard sandbox. For example, in the App Orchard sandbox, if searching for Progress Notes: type=1.2.840.114350.1.13.0.1.7.4.737880.5010|1

In Epic, coverage records exhibit the following characteristics: The patient-level coverage list represents all possible insurances that could be billed for services. A patient might have a long list of possible coverages that are applicable only for specific services. Examples include third party liability, workers' comp, black lung insurance, Medicaid for ESRD, Medicare, commercial, and others. For any specific visit, an account record will indicate which coverages will be used for that visit. A single visit-level account may have multiple coverages attached. Coverage filing order indicates which is billed first. Coverages may be specific to service area. For this reason, if you are searching across multiple service areas, a patient might have what appears to be duplicate coverages. This resource typically should not be used to determine which coverages are relevant for recent or upcoming visits and services. Instead, it returns all coverages that are potentially applicable to a patient. This resource respects patient-level break-the-glass checks as configured in Epic. Retrieves a Coverage resource by its FHIR ID. Coverage resources correspond to coverage records in Epic. In Epic, coverage records exhibit the following characteristics: The patient-level coverage list represents all possible insurances that could be billed for services. A patient might have a long list of possible coverages that are applicable only for specific services. Examples include third party liability, worker's comp, black lung insurance, Medicaid for ESRD, Medicare, commercial, etc. For any specific visit, an account record will indicate which coverages will be used for that visit. A single visit-level account may have multiple coverages attached. Coverage filing order indicates which is billed first. Coverages are specific to service area. For this reason, if you are searching across multiple service areas, a patient might have what appears to be duplicate coverages. This resource typically should not be used to determine which coverages are relevant for recent or upcoming visits and services. Instead, it returns all coverages that are potentially applicable to a patient. This resource respects patient-level break-the-glass checks as configured in Epic. Audit events are logged to the patient audit trail when a coverage is accessed by this resource.When things go wrong, the API will respond with an error code and a human-readable description to describe the incorrect submission. Currently, the error code is not included in the REST version of the specification, but it is provided here for your reference. These codes are meant for developer use only - they should not be presented to end users. Instead, your application should interpret the codes and provide user-friendly resolution steps when data cannot be filed. FHIR Errors come in two flavors: Fatal Errors cause the response to contain no results and are usually due to requests from the client processed as invalid - missing or invalid data in the request, unauthorized access, or expired content in the system. Warning Errors accompany a successful response and are used to indicate that part of a request could not be fulfilled - for example, if a status is unknown, but the request can be fulfilled, the API will return the data and indicate that part of the request couldn't be understood.

The FHIR Device resource describes information about durable, manufactured medical items. Starting in November 2021, this resource supports both implantable and external medical devices. UDI device identifier.  Under FDA regulations, all medical devices are required to include a Unique Device Identifier (UDI) on device labels and packages, in both human-readable and barcode format. The FDA also maintains a public database of medical devices and UDI information called the Global Unique Device Identification Database (GUDID).  A Unique Device Identifier (UDI) is a unique numeric or alphanumeric code that is comprised of two components:  Device Identifier (DI) ("Static UDI") – a mandatory, fixed portion of a UDI that identifiers the labeler and specific version or model of a device. Production Identifiers (PI) ("Dynamic UDI") – a conditional, variable portion of a UDI that identifies one or more of the following: Lot or batch number within which a device was manufactured Serial number of a specific device Expiration date of a specific device Production date of a specific device Distinct identification code for a human cell, tissue, or cellular- and tissue-based product When documenting a UDI for an implant in OpTime, you will need to use an identifier that is in a valid format for the selected issuer. Here are some example UDIs you can use for testing:  UDI Type / Issuer	Example Device ID ICCBBA	W4184228005T0473 HIBC	MDLXMAG120200 GS1	00822409025305
Patient identifier for the patient to whom the device is affixed.

In Epic, clinical pathways are diagnosis- or surgery-specific protocols that are organized into sequential steps. These steps contain orders, patient outcomes, and clinical documentation elements that represent the care that will be provided and goals for the patient for that stage of care or day of the admission. The Consent.Search interaction returns only metadata about the patient consent document(s) on file, such as the type of consent and the effective period.
